name: Lake Mountain

facts.claim: Lake Mountain is a 1,433 m peak on a plateau about 120 km north-east of Melbourne, home to a cross-country ski resort of the same name
The resort has a 37 km ski trail network through Yarra Ranges National Park and is popular with families for snow play and tobogganing
In summer it offers mountain biking, with runs descending 30 km from the top to Marysville, plus bushwalks and boardwalks

access_note: Summer entry is free 7 days a week with facilities closed; snow-season day-visitor entry and trail/toboggan pass prices were not clearly extractable (winter page lists $69, $33, $29 etc. products).

name: Marysville

facts.claim: Marysville is a town about 96 km east of Melbourne, established in 1863 as a stopover for diggers heading to the goldfields
Almost the entire town was destroyed in the 2009 Black Saturday bushfires and has since been rebuilt
It is the base for Lake Mountain, Steavenson Falls and walks into Yarra Ranges National Park

name: Steavenson Falls

facts.claim: Steavenson Falls is a waterfall on the Steavenson River, 4 km south-east of Marysville, with five cascades and a total descent of about 122 m (sources vary 82-122 m)
The 190 ha Steavenson Falls Scenic Reserve protects the falls, with walks from easy to harder
The path and falls are floodlit at night, powered by a small turbine generator
A 3.4 km Tree Fern Gully Trail leads from Marysville

facts.claim: Warburton is a town in the Shire of Yarra Ranges, 76 km east of Melbourne
The former Lilydale branch railway is now the Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail for walkers, cyclists and horse riders
It sits on the Yarra River and is a gateway to the ranges east of the Yarra Valley
The Black Spur is a 30 km stretch of the Maroondah Highway between Healesville and Narbethong
The road winds through tall mountain ash (Eucalyptus regnans) forest, with the Dom Dom Saddle picnic area on the way
It is the usual drive from Melbourne to Marysville and Lake Mountain

name: Keppel Falls

facts.claim: Keppel Falls is in Yarra Ranges National Park, reached from Lady Talbot Drive, about a 20-minute drive from Marysville
A walk from the Keppel Falls Walk car park follows the track over a footbridge through ferns to where the Taggerty River cascades over boulders
The track can be boggy and inaccessible to two-wheel-drive cars in wet weather

access_note: Roads can be boggy in wet weather; access may vary while works are underway.
